text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bahraini press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bahrain aims to be a major industrial force in the region and the government is taking serious measures to achieve this goal, oil and industry minister says.
- Bahrain-based Investcorp signs an agreement to buy Norwegian outdoor and sportswear company Helly Hansen.
- Flights between Bahrain and India returned to normal on Saturday after Indian air traffic controllers called off a two-day strike.
- A major kidney and liver transplant centre may soon be set up in Bahrain.
- Morocco plans two products and services exhibitions in Bahrain this year to boost exports. Moroccan exports to Bahrain in 1996 climbed to $644,317 from $389,529 a year earlier.
- Bahrain University allocates 500,000 dinars to cover its employees salary rise of 15 percent.
- A Bahraini trade team leaves for Germany to participate in Hanover International Exhibition.
- Bahrain Kuwait Insurance Company to pay 17 percent dividend to shareholders.
- Bahrain allocates $50 million to develop its oil refinery, oil and industry minister says.
